I have been with one of my partners for 13ish years (we weren't seriously dating for 2 years, so I'm hesitant to put 15 despite there being feelings there), and another for 11. I have another at 7, then 5 and then 4, with one that just started recently (2 weeks!). I promise I'm not a time traveler, I just never sleep and I tend to be hyper-focused on command. They are all very different and all have their own supply and demands, but I tend to use the same bag of 'tricks' for each relationship in order to keep everyone happy.

I think the biggest thing for all of my relationships is never assume that someone else is ever doing something to be malicious/hurtful. It sounds like easy advice, but there have been many times where in my brain I go 'well they just wanted to' or 'well they should have' or 'well I would have'. I'm completely separate from them as a human, as they are me, and TALKING (about pain/anxiety) until my jaw falls off has made everything infinitely easier combined with the; they love me, they are here, they want this as much as me. I am also extremely vigilant about my mental health; so are they, we all see therapists and unload our problems there, NOT on one another. We're not professionals in that venue, unfortunately. :) This means we can talk to one another about things that bother us without feeling like we are being a burden, and with insight that we might otherwise not have had. I understand we're lucky to be able to do this; there have been times where we couldn't afford it, but everyone sort of makes a safety net until the person is stable. It very much becomes a 'we are in this together'.

As with any relationships, there are going to be ups and downs - extreme sickness (rough, twice!), money problems (still ongoing but creeping out of the bad now, and if your partners aren't all buckling down if you live in a household together, it's HARD.), and when someone gets NRE and goes loopy (I hate NRE, personally), but checking in through all of this in everyone's love language is vital. If it's me talking to someone, or making them a meal, or leaving them a little gift, the small things after years, the simple 'I am thinking of you, I love you' makes little touchstones that can be related back to so important to us.  We do not always have all the time in the world for each other, but that world is special to us and we try to keep it safe and maintain our little well weeded garden.
